welcome_lead: Trace atomic radius, IE and electronegativity across Period 3.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Across a period: nuclear charge rises but shielding ~constant, so outer e- pulled closer.

Down a group: more shells, outer e- further from nucleus, radius increases.

General rise from Na to Ar, but two dips: Al (3p starts, easier to remove) and S (3p4 has paired e- repelling).

Trend: Na < Mg > Al > Si < P > S < Cl < Ar in order of IE values.

Na, Mg, Al: metallic, mp increases with charge density. Si: giant covalent, very high mp.

P4, S8, Cl2, Ar: simple molecular, mp drops sharply; depends on London force size. S8 > P4 > Cl2 > Ar.

mcqs.q: Why does Al have lower 1st IE than Mg?
options: 3p electron easier to remove than 3s
Al has more shielding from core
Mg has more protons
Al is more reactive

mcqs.q: Why does atomic radius increase down a group?
options: Atoms get bigger down a group because nuclei swell when they have more neutrons.
Each successive element has an additional electron shell, increasing the distance of outer electrons from the nucleus.
Atoms get bigger down a group because they have more protons attracting more matter.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.

mcqs.q: Why does first ionisation energy generally increase across a period?
options: Because d orbitals can only fill after p orbitals in the next shell.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
Atoms get bigger across a period, making electrons easier to add but harder to remove.
Nuclear charge increases while shielding stays roughly constant, so electrons are held more tightly.

mcqs.q: Why is the 4s orbital filled before the 3d orbital?
options: Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
Because the 4s orbital has a lower energy than 3d when both are empty, so electrons fill it first.
Because d orbitals can only fill after p orbitals in the next shell.
Because the 4s shell is closer to the nucleus than the 3d shell.
